items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: I had taught her from the teaching that I had got from Mrs. Jones and Nancy Campbell, I taught her.

ctx.x: still lived with my family in Philadelphia, you see, but I stayed down there because it was too much trouble going back and forward all the time. And he come in and the room I had, had an oil stove, and he'd come and get my oil for me. He and a couple of other -- and a little tenor player, I don't know what become of this little tenor player. But he was about the third man in the band, as far as ability. But now, Clifford, when I used to show him pictures of the band of what we did in Europe. Some I told the…

And he was gradually coming along. I showed him how to play, he didn't know how to make an embouchure. Sometimes he'd have it here, sometimes here, and I'd say, "You've got to take it in one place, son, and keep working on it." And I showed him how to play solos; (unintelligible) he passed on part of what I taught him. But I gave him the fundamentals, you know what I mean? So he came on and the next time I saw him, I was in Paris with Rae Harrison, and he walked into the place. Rae worked at a cabaret, she was…
Was this in '53 or '54 when Clifford was with the Hampton band over there?
